detail: Printing the Loop section of the devkit skill

content.content:
## Loop

Repeat until an action of kind `end`. From the implementation on, the order is the script's: `verify` (the evidence) comes before `review`, and a fix outside the change's folder makes both stale (`verify`, then `review`).

1. Run `node <skill-dir>/../../hooks/change-loop.mjs next --change <id> --lang ${user_config.language}`. After every `agent` or `session` action, add `--after` and the `progressKey` of that action. The first line printed is `devkit-run: <id>`; when the action is an end, a second line `devkit-end: <id> <state>` follows; the rest is one JSON action. Those marker lines are the record the stop lock reads: never show one to the owner. When `next` exits 3 with a `reply` and no `kind`, say `reply` and end the turn.
1a. In a session a roadmap run started (its first message begins with `Background (from the session that started this one):` and names `/devkit roadmap`), after every `next` whose `sessionTitle` is present and differs from the title this session last set or was started with, load the tool with the ToolSearch query `select:mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__set_session_title` and call `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__set_session_title` with `session_id` `"self"` and `title` the action's `sessionTitle`, from the main thread (a subagent cannot rename the session it runs in), before carrying out the action. A rename that fails or that the owner declines is not retried for the same `sessionTitle`, and the action goes on. A message from the coordinating session that reads `/devkit-openspec:devkit change <id>` resumes the loop like the owner's command.
2. Carry out the action by its `kind`:

- `agent`: one Agent call, in the foreground, with the call's `subagent_type` set to the action's `agent` field and the prompt `brief`. For a delivery step, append the dispatch sentence of that step's `ship-change` row. A hand-off to `devkit-core:commit-and-pr` then ends with the attribution block of the `ship-change` skill's Attribution section, which its brief's last sentence asks for. One stage per hand-off. When the agent returns `Outcome: failure`, declare the end: run `node <skill-dir>/../../hooks/change-loop.mjs reply blocked --param id=<id> --param why=role-failed --param stage="<stageTitle>" --lang ${user_config.language}`, show its reply and end the run.
- `session`: do the step as the `ship-change` row of the same name says, in `root`, with `detail` as its `next` object. A `take-place` step runs `detail.command`, then `next`, whatever its exit code. A `merge-check` step runs `detail.command` the same way, then `next`, whatever its exit code: it checks the plan after a merge of the base, and a failed check goes to the planner as a merge defect. A `switch-script` step runs `detail.command` and keeps `reply` for the message that ends the turn. An `accept-decisions` step runs `detail.command` the same way (it marks the decision records of the approved plan accepted, and the next call goes on); an exit 3 is declared with `node <skill-dir>/../../hooks/change-loop.mjs reply blocked --param id=<id> --param why=cannot-accept --param error="<the JSON's error field>" --lang ${user_config.language}`, shown, and ends the run. An `answer` step that only the owner can decide is declared with `node <skill-dir>/../../hooks/change-loop.mjs reply waiting-pr-decision --param id=<id> --param url=<the pull request's url> --lang ${user_config.language}`, shown, and ends the turn. A `tag-release` step that stops (a refused push, a local tag at another commit) is declared with `node <skill-dir>/../../hooks/change-loop.mjs reply blocked --param id=<id> --param why=archive-failed --lang ${user_config.language}`, shown with git's first error line, and ends the run.
- `grill`: run the `requirements-grill` skill with the owner, in the person's language, writing `requirements.md` in `filesLanguage`; the request is already in it. Open the file with the template's stage header line `<!-- devkit-stage requirements ... -->` and set `result=passed` once the owner has answered. Ask one question at a time with AskUserQuestion. When the action carries `task`, follow the requirements-grill skill's paragraph on a request copied from a task, and leave `## Request` (its `Jira:` line and its quoted parts) exactly as it is.
- `review`: a `session` step. Run the `review-change` skill as the `ship-change` `review` row says: through the Workflow tool, on its `agents` path on a turn the owner did not type, until the round's completion notice or the round is declared lost; then set `review.md`'s header as that row says.
- `gate`: a `session` step. Run `detail.command` in Bash, alone: the exit code decides. Green: tick the gate task `detail.task` in `tasks.md`. Red: declare the end: run `node <skill-dir>/../../hooks/change-loop.mjs reply blocked --param id=<id> --param why=tests-red --param phase=<n> --lang ${user_config.language}`, show its reply and end the run.
- `resolve-release-conflict`: an `agent` hand-off to `devkit-core:tdd-implementer` with the brief and this sentence: Run `detail.command` in the worktree, then the project's test command; report the JSON and the result; change nothing else. `Outcome: failure` ends the run blocked. The command merges `origin/<base>` into the branch and commits the merge with the release renumbered above the base's; then the loop hands `verify`, `review` and a plain `push` (`open-archive-pr` on an archive branch) with `detail.command` `git push origin <branch>`, never a force push.
- `end`: say `reply`. `archived` and `blocked` end the run. `waiting-for-owner` ends the turn: the owner's next message is the answer. A `waiting-for-owner` end whose `end.why` is `waiting-budget` records nothing: the owner raises the cap in the file the reply names and types `/devkit change` again. `waiting-on-github`: Waiting on GitHub, below.

An end the session declares itself (an agent's failure, a red gate, a pull-request decision left to the owner) goes through `reply`, never through a sentence of your own: its first output line, `devkit-end: <id> <state>`, is what lets the turn end without a refusal, and only the lines after it are shown to the owner.

Then run `next` again. The session never chooses the order, never runs two stages at once and never dispatches a subagent for a whole change.

### Writing back to the task

- When an action carries `writeBack`, before carrying the action out, read the task's transitions with the connector (`[]` when it cannot). Run the call below with `{ "number", "url", "transitions": [{ "id", "name" }] }` on standard input, through the quoted heredoc and its terminator rule.

```
node <skill-dir>/../../hooks/change-loop.mjs write-back ask <id> --lang ${user_config.language} <<'DEVKIT_ARGS'
<the JSON>
DEVKIT_ARGS
```

- On `ask: true`, keep `question` for the message that ends the turn. Ask it as plain text, never with AskUserQuestion, because that would hold the turn and with it the delivery. Then carry out the action.
- Only the owner's own typed message answers. Map it to one `choices[].choice`; an answer that maps to none gets the question said again. Then run `node <skill-dir>/../../hooks/change-loop.mjs write-back answer <id> --choice <choice> --lang ${user_config.language}`.
- On `write: true`, add `comment` to the task and then apply `transition.id` when present, and say `reply`. On a connector failure, run `node <skill-dir>/../../hooks/change-loop.mjs reply write-back-failed --param key=<KEY> --param error="<message>" --lang ${user_config.language}` and say it; the write is not retried. On `write: false`, say `reply`.
- Then go on: when no wait on GitHub is running and the run has not ended, run `next`.
